f.title: Treat spontaneously reported events as ADRs even when relationship is unknown
f.statement: For regulatory reporting purposes, an event that is spontaneously reported meets the definition of an adverse drug reaction even if the relationship is unknown or unstated.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: For regulatory reporting purposes, if an event is spontaneously reported, even if the relationship is unknown or unstated, it meets the definition of an adverse drug reaction.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. Definition; Recommended level is a judgement.

f.title: Classify an AE/ADR as serious when it meets an ICH E2A seriousness criterion
f.statement: In accordance with ICH E2A, a serious adverse event or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening (the patient was at risk of death at the time of the event/reaction, not one that hypothetically might have caused death if more severe), requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongs existing hospitalisation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, or is a medically important event or reaction.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: In accordance with the ICH E2A guideline, a serious adverse event or reaction is any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose: * results in death, * is life-threatening (NOTE: The term “life-threatening” in the definition of “serious” refers to an event/reaction in which the patient was at risk of death at the time of the event/reaction; it does not refer to an event/ reaction which hypothetically might have caused death if it were more severe), * requires inpatient hospitalisation or results in prolongation of existing hospitalisation, * results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, 1 Post-Approval Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting * is a congenital anomaly/birth defect, * is a medically important event or reaction.
rows.review_note: Review: Quote spans a page break and so contains the page footer/header ("1 Post-Approval Safety Data Management..."); it cannot be re-cut without losing two seriousness criteria, so kept. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. Quote contains the page footer ('1 Post-Approval Safety Data Management: ...') inside the list; definition only.

f.title: Use medical and scientific judgement to consider important medical events serious
f.statement: Medical and scientific judgement should be exercised in deciding whether other situations, such as important medical events that might not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but might jeopardise the patient or require intervention to prevent another serious outcome, should be considered serious (e.g. intensive treatment for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions without hospitalisation, development of drug dependency or abuse).
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: Medical and scientific judgment should be exercised in deciding whether other situations should be considered serious such as important medical events that might not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation but might jeopardise the patient or might require intervention to prevent one of the other outcomes listed in the definition above. Examples of such events are intensive treatment in an emergency room or at home for allergic bronchospasm, blood dyscrasias or convulsions that do not result in hospitalization, or development of drug dependency or drug abuse.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. ICH guideline wording; actor (MAH) implied.

f.title: Treat ADRs inconsistent with local/regional labelling as unexpected; when uncertain, treat as unexpected
f.statement: An ADR whose nature, severity, specificity or outcome is not consistent with the term or description in the local/regional product labelling (e.g. Package Insert or SmPC) should be considered unexpected. When the MAH is uncertain whether an ADR is expected or unexpected, it should be treated as unexpected.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: An ADR whose nature, severity, specificity, or outcome is not consistent with the term or description used in the local/regional product labeling (e.g. Package Insert or Summary of Product Characteristics) should be considered unexpected. When a Marketing Authorisation Holder (MAH) is uncertain whether an ADR is expected or unexpected, the ADR should be treated as unexpected.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. ICH guideline wording; actor (MAH) implied.

f.title: Treat an expected ADR with a fatal outcome as unexpected unless labelling mentions fatal outcome
f.statement: An expected ADR with a fatal outcome should be considered unexpected unless the local/regional product labelling specifically states that the ADR might be associated with a fatal outcome.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: An expected ADR with a fatal outcome should be considered unexpected unless the local/regional product labeling specifically states that the ADR might be associated with a fatal outcome.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. ICH guideline wording; actor (MAH) implied.

f.title: Consider class ADRs expected only if labelling describes them as occurring with the product
f.statement: "Class ADRs" should not automatically be considered expected for the subject drug; they should be considered expected only if described as specifically occurring with the product in the local/regional product labelling. Where labelling only states that other drugs of the class are reported to cause the ADR (or that no reports have been received with the drug), the ADR should not be considered expected for that drug.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: “Class ADRs” should not automatically be considered to be expected for the subject drug. “Class ADRs” should be considered expected only if described as specifically occurring with the product in the local/regional product labeling. This is illustrated in the following examples: • “As with other drugs of this class, the following undesirable effect occurs with Drug X.” • “Drugs of this class, including Drug X, can cause...” If the ADR has not been documented with Drug X, statements such as the following are likely to appear in the local/regional product labeling: • “Other drugs of this class are reported to cause…” • “Drugs of this class are reported to cause..., but no reports have been received to date with Drug X.” In these situations, the ADR should not be considered as expected for Drug X.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: superseded/draft version; no previous_key link to the current baseline. ICH guideline wording; actor (MAH) implied.

f.title: Use listedness against the CCSI, not for expedited reporting
f.statement: The term "listedness" is not applicable to expedited reporting but should be used to characterise the ADR according to the Company Core Safety Information (see ICH E2C).
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: NOTE: The term “listedness” is not applicable to expedited reporting but should be used to characterize the ADR according to the Company Core Safety Information (refer to ICH E2C guideline for definitions).

f.title: Classify reporters as healthcare professionals or consumers per the definitions
f.statement: A healthcare professional is a medically-qualified person such as a physician, dentist, pharmacist, nurse, coroner, or as otherwise specified by local regulations; a consumer is a person who is not a healthcare professional, such as a patient, lawyer, friend or relative of a patient.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety intake & collection

f.title: Consider stimulated reports spontaneous
f.statement: Reports stimulated, for example, by a "Dear Healthcare Professional" letter, press publication or questioning of healthcare professionals by company representatives should be considered spontaneous.

f.title: Handle consumer reports as spontaneous irrespective of medical confirmation and retain them
f.statement: Consumer adverse reaction reports should be handled as spontaneous reports irrespective of any subsequent medical confirmation (regulatory authorities might require medical confirmation for expedited reporting). Emphasis should be placed on the quality of the report rather than its source, and cases from consumers should be retained even if they do not qualify for regulatory reporting.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

f.title: Screen worldwide scientific literature regularly, at least every two weeks or per local requirements
f.statement: Each MAH is expected to regularly screen the worldwide scientific literature by accessing widely used systematic literature reviews or reference databases. The frequency of literature searches should be according to local requirements or at least every two weeks.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

f.title: Assess literature ADR cases, including abstracts and draft manuscripts, for expedited reporting
f.statement: Cases of ADRs from the scientific and medical literature, including relevant published abstracts from meetings and draft manuscripts, might qualify for expedited reporting.

f.title: Provide one regulatory reporting form per identifiable patient in literature cases, citing the publication as source
f.statement: A regulatory reporting form with relevant medical information should be provided for each identifiable patient. The publication reference(s) should be given as the report source; the local regulatory authority might also request a copy of the article to accompany the report.

f.title: Company offices to watch local journals and alert the safety department
f.statement: All company offices are encouraged to be aware of publications in their local journals and to bring them to the attention of the company safety department as appropriate.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

f.title: Assume an unbranded literature product is the MAH's own, noting brand not identified

f.title: Only the MAH whose product the author suspects reports a multi-product literature case

For Internet cases (e.g. e-mail), reporter identifiability refers to the existence of a real person, i.e. it is possible to verify that the patient and reporter exist.

f.statement: Solicited reports derive from organised data collection systems (clinical trials, registries, post-approval named patient use programmes, patient support and disease management programmes, surveys of patients or healthcare providers, information gathering on efficacy or compliance); adverse event reports obtained from any of these should not be considered spontaneous.

f.title: Specify safety information exchange, timelines and reporting responsibilities in contractual agreements
f.statement: In licensing/contractual relationships, explicit agreements should specify the processes for exchange of safety information, including timelines and regulatory reporting responsibilities, and safety personnel should be involved in developing any agreement from the beginning.

f.title: Communicate other observations that could change the risk-benefit evaluation as soon as possible
f.statement: Any safety information from other observations that could change the product's risk-benefit evaluation should be communicated as soon as possible to the regulatory authorities in accordance with local regulation, e.g. significant unanticipated findings from in vitro, animal, epidemiological or clinical studies suggesting significant human risk (mutagenicity, teratogenicity, carcinogenicity, or lack of efficacy with a drug for a life-threatening or serious disease).
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: In addition to single case reports, any safety information from other observations that could change the risk-benefit evaluation for the product should be communicated as soon as possible to the regulatory authorities in accordance with local regulation. f.title: Discuss lack of efficacy in the PSUR; consider expediting for certain product classes
f.statement: Evidence of lack of efficacy should not normally be expedited but should be discussed in the relevant PSUR. In certain circumstances and regions individual reports are subject to expedited reporting; for products treating life-threatening or serious diseases, vaccines and contraceptives, lack of efficacy should be considered for expedited reporting, using clinical judgement with consideration of local labelling and the disease treated.
f.applicability: Superseded version (replaced by ICH E2D(R1), Step 4 15 Sep 2025). ICH E2D Step 4 of 12 Nov 2003; post-approval safety data and expedited reporting.

rows.quote: Evidence of lack of efficacy should not normally be expedited, but should be discussed in the relevant periodic safety update report. Medicinal products used for the treatment of life-threatening or serious diseases, vaccines, and contraceptives are examples of classes of medicinal products where lack of efficacy should be considered for expedited reporting. Clinical judgment should be used in reporting, with consideration of the local product labeling and disease being treated.
